readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant send a phone reminder before each timed appointment, including simultaneous events, without unexpected all-day alerts?
directAnswer: Use the event's calendar trigger with a -15-minute start offset, queued mode and trigger.calendar_event data. Exclude all-day events, test plain phone delivery first, then create two harmless timed appointments far enough ahead for polling. This example does not replay reminders missed during downtime.
originalContribution: Sections 3 and 4 provide a complete built-in automation with separate in-interface and phone outputs, plus an original 14:00 setup / 15:00 dual-appointment / 14:45 reminder rehearsal. The decision table distinguishes absent calendar data, no trigger, all-day exclusion, and phone delivery failure. It also checks duplicate notification replacement separately from missing calendar triggers.
limitations: Documentation and Home Assistant 2026.9.4 source research; no live Home Assistant installation, physical phone, provider synchronization, or notification latency test was performed. YAML parsing and Jinja rendering used synthetic timed, simultaneous, all-day and UTC event fixtures, not an integration runtime. No guarantee of delivery, catch-up, immediate event-edit propagation, or offline phone push. Generated cover is labeled editorial illustration.

claimChecks.claim: Calendar events should trigger reminders individually; a negative start offset fires before the event, and calendars are read every 15 minutes. The original test gives 45 minutes before the offset trigger.
The trigger exposes calendar_event.summary, start and all_day. The example filters all-day events and reads per-run event data rather than the single next-event entity attribute.
Queued mode preserves arrival order and max counts active plus queued runs. Long waits would delay later notifications; reaching the configured maximum can reject additional runs.
Run actions omits trigger data and skips top-level conditions, so it is not a valid end-to-end test for this calendar recipe. Future real test events and traces are the prescribed verification.
All-day dates are interpreted at local midnight; excluding them prevents the -15-minute trigger from sending a previous-evening alert. A separate 09:15 timed entry gives a 09:00 reminder.

The checked implementation starts scheduling at the current/future window, fetches batches, and has no persistent delivery ledger for this automation. Downtime and last-minute event edits are explicitly limited.
Phone notifications use a phone-specific notify.mobile_app action and require notification permission plus a message. Shared notification tags can replace prior alerts; this recipe does not use one.
persistent_notification.create produces an in-interface message; omitting a fixed notification_id allows separate messages. That action is not a phone-delivery receipt.
timestamp_custom with local_time true formats the parsed event timestamp in Home Assistant's configured time zone; synthetic UTC and local fixtures rendered the same appointment time.
Time zone is currently under Settings > System > Home information > Region; General is identified as older UI wording.
Local calendar event storage does not establish offline phone delivery. Local Push has separate app/connection requirements.
Standard push may involve external delivery services. Appointment titles copied into Home Assistant and phone notifications require attention to shared displays and lock-screen previews.
Google Calendar integration requires account authorization and configured developer credentials; it is an alternative event source, not an automatic copy of Local calendar.
